ANA.name: Anaheim Ducks
text: The Ducks are 4-3-0 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not. Early days, of course.
Night to night, they play fast, wide-open games and crash the net for second chances.

BOS.name: Boston Bruins
text: The Bruins are 6-2-0 so far, winners of four straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in six of their eight games. Early days, of course.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and shoot from distance.
They spend a lot of time in the box, but their goaltending has been stealing games.

BUF.name: Buffalo Sabres
text: The Sabres are 4-3-1 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not. It’s early, mind you.
Their game? They find a way to get their shots past the blockers and rarely block shots.

CGY.name: Calgary Flames
text: The rebuild grinds on in Calgary: no playoffs in four seasons, and a 1-6-0 start.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Night to night, they fire from everywhere, though a lot of it is hopeful and let the other team shoot a lot.
Their power play has no bite and their goaltending has let them down.

CAR.name: Carolina Hurricanes
text: The defending champs are picking up right where they left off, 6-1-1 out of the gate, winners of six straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in six of their eight games. Early days, of course.
Expect them to give up very few shots, though the ones they allow are dangerous and push out to take away the point shot.
They create chances even when shorthanded and their penalty kill is airtight.

CHI.name: Chicago Blackhawks
text: The rebuild grinds on in Chicago: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 3-5-0 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that. Early days, of course.
Their game? They spend a lot of the night in their own end and shoot from distance.
Their power play has no bite.

COL.name: Colorado Avalanche
text: Same old Avalanche: 5-2-1, and in the mix again.
And it’s no mirage: they’ve had the better of the chances in seven of their eight games. It’s early, mind you.
Night to night, they shoot from distance and play fast, wide-open games.
Their penalty kill is airtight and they stay out of the box.

CBJ.name: Columbus Blue Jackets
text: The rebuild grinds on in Columbus: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 2-3-0 start.
The results haven’t come yet, but they’ve had the better of the chances most nights, so don’t write them off.
On the ice, they send their defensemen in to shoot and get to the dangerous chances.
Their penalty kill leaks.

DAL.name: Dallas Stars
text: The Stars, playoff regulars, are 3-3-1 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not. Small sample, sure.
On the ice, they get in front of a lot of shots and grind games down.
Their power play is lethal and their penalty kill is airtight.

DET.name: Detroit Red Wings
text: The rebuild grinds on in Detroit: no playoffs in ten seasons, and a 2-3-2 start.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Night to night, they get in front of a lot of shots and give up dangerous chances.
They stay out of the box and their power play is lethal.

EDM.name: Edmonton Oilers
text: The Oilers are 5-1-1, which is what we’ve come to expect.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and lean hard on their top players.
Their power play is lethal and they create chances even when shorthanded.

FLA.name: Florida Panthers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Panthers have bounced back to 4-2-2.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in five of their eight games. Small sample, sure.
Night to night, they rarely block shots and hound the puck in the other team’s end.
Their power play is lethal.

LAK.name: Los Angeles Kings
text: The Kings have made the playoffs five years running, but they’re 0-3-2 this time, losers of five straight.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Expect them to settle for a lot of hopeful shots and keep the other team to hopeful shots.
Their goaltending has let them down.

MIN.name: Minnesota Wild
text: The Wild are 5-2-1 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and get pinned in their own end on long shifts.
Their goaltending has been stealing games and they stay out of the box.

MTL.name: Montréal Canadiens
text: The Canadiens are 3-3-1 so far.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not. It’s early, mind you.
On the ice, they get into a lot of chippy games and give up dangerous chances.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

NSH.name: Nashville Predators
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Predators are 2-2-3, losers of three straight.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not. It’s early, mind you.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble.

NJD.name: New Jersey Devils
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Devils are 4-4-0.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not. Small sample, sure.
Night to night, they spend most of the night in the other team’s end and pounce on turnovers.

NYI.name: New York Islanders
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Islanders are 3-3-1.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not. It’s early, mind you.
Night to night, they send their defensemen in to shoot and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their penalty kill leaks.

NYR.name: New York Rangers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Rangers have bounced back to 6-3-0.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they get a lot of their shots blocked and get right to the net.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

OTT.name: Ottawa Senators
text: The Senators are 6-2-0 so far.
Don’t get too comfortable, though: they’ve been outchanced in most of those games, and that tends to catch up with a team.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.
They stay out of the box and they create chances even when shorthanded.

PHI.name: Philadelphia Flyers
text: The Flyers are 0-6-3 so far, losers of nine straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that. It’s early, mind you.
Their game? They spend a lot of the night in their own end and pounce on turnovers.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

PIT.name: Pittsburgh Penguins
text: The Penguins are 3-4-1 so far.
The results haven’t come yet, but they’ve had the better of the chances most nights, so don’t write them off.
Their game? They get right to the net and sit back rather than forecheck.

SJS.name: San Jose Sharks
text: The Sharks are 4-3-0, still looking for their first playoff spot in seven seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not. Small sample, sure.
Their game? They ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble and get a lot of their shots blocked.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

SEA.name: Seattle Kraken
text: Could this be the year? The Kraken haven’t made the playoffs in three seasons, but they’re 5-2-1 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Expect them to let the other team shoot, but mostly hopeful shots and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.

STL.name: St. Louis Blues
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Blues are 3-3-1.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not. Early days, of course.
Night to night, they get to the dangerous chances and keep things calm after the whistle.
Their power play has no bite.

TBL.name: Tampa Bay Lightning
text: Same old Lightning: 5-2-0, and in the mix again.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in five of their seven games. Early days, of course.
Expect them to get into a lot of chippy games and spend most of the night in the other team’s end.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

TOR.name: Toronto Maple Leafs
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Maple Leafs are 3-3-2.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not. It’s early, mind you.
On the ice, they pounce on turnovers and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

UTA.name: Utah Mammoth
text: The Mammoth are 6-2-0 so far, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in seven of their eight games. Small sample, sure.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and collapse around the net and give up the point.

VAN.name: Vancouver Canucks
text: Last season was one to forget in Vancouver, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 2-6-1, losers of six straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that. Early days, of course.
Expect them to crash the net for second chances and give up dangerous chances.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

VGK.name: Vegas Golden Knights
text: Last spring’s runners-up look hungry: they’re 7-2-0.
And it’s no mirage: they’ve had the better of the chances in seven of their nine games. Early days, of course.
Expect them to push out to take away the point shot and send their defensemen in to shoot.
Their penalty kill is airtight and they stay out of the box.

WSH.name: Washington Capitals
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Capitals have bounced back to 5-3-0.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Their game? They get to the dangerous chances and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their power play has no bite.

WPG.name: Winnipeg Jets
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Jets have bounced back to 4-1-2.
Don’t get too comfortable, though: they’ve been outchanced in most of those games, and that tends to catch up with a team.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and settle for a lot of hopeful shots.
